results.name: actor_dispatch_look_handler_by_posture
results.evidence: Early-outs unless a posture value (unaff_BX) is 0 or 1, calls actor_get_actor_definition, then dispatches through function-pointer table PTR_LAB_0041be00 indexed by a stack short; called from actor_danger_update (0x41eda0) with 6 args including a position.
results.summary: Validates a posture/type index (0 or 1), then dispatches through a jump table of handler functions selected by another index, after fetching the actor's definition; actor index and args are passed in registers/stack, unclear beyond that.

results.name: actor_target_get_priority_class
results.evidence: Classifies a target-data record (stride 0x138 off DAT_008802c0) into 0-3 based on combat state field +0x24 in [2,3], seat state +0x66 in {1,2}, exposure +0x60, and death flag +0x127, with a fallback based on awareness fields +0x6a/+0x6e of the actor record (stride 0x724 off DAT_00880360).
results.summary: Given an actor index (EAX) and optional target-data index (ECX), returns a small integer priority class (0-3) describing how urgent/visible that target currently is.

results.name: unit_get_move_speed_for_range
results.evidence: Pure float math with no side effects: reads move-speed thresholds at unit-type-record+0x1c/0x20/0x28/0x2c and interpolates forward/turn speed outputs into *param_4/*param_5 based on distance param_3.
results.summary: Computes interpolated forward and turn movement speeds for a unit's move-speed profile at a given target distance, writing the results through param_4 and param_5.

results.name: actor_target_hearing_check
results.evidence: Computes squared planar distance between two positions, scales a hearing radius by crouch/stealth checks (calls to FUN_0053e810 twice) and posture (param_2), then compares against cluster_sound_distance_lookup's returned radius to decide audibility.
results.summary: Determines whether a target at a given position is within the actor's effective hearing radius, accounting for stealth/crouch state and ambient sound-cluster noise level.

results.name: actor_find_nearest_squad_target
results.evidence: Iterates either the actor's linked target-object chain (object+0x1fc) or an encounter-squad member array (DAT_0088035c, stride 0x98) computing squared distance to param_1's position via object_get_position, applying a 0.36x bias for the object matching param_2 and 2.25x for flagged members, returning the closest index.
results.summary: Searches the actor's linked target list or its encounter squad for the object nearest to a given position, with distance biases favoring/penalizing certain candidates, and optionally stamps a 'last seen' timestamp on each visited object.

results.name: actor_target_data_refresh
results.evidence: Revalidates a target-data record's tracked object, reassigning it via actor_find_nearest_squad_target (0x41c2c0) for squad-shared targets, then refetches node transforms via object_get_node_local_transform for barrel/aim markers and root-object bounding data via object_get_root_object_index.
results.summary: Refreshes a target-data record (actor param_1 / target index param_2) by re-resolving its tracked object when appropriate and recomputing cached aim-node transforms and object bounding info.

results.name: actor_target_update_tracking_speed
results.evidence: Calls object_get_velocity-style helper (FUN_004f6aa0) and buckets the resulting speed magnitude into 0-3 at target-data+0x123 using fixed thresholds (0.0033/0.0167/0.0333), and similarly buckets a closing-speed dot product into target-data+0x124; large body truncated (423 lines not shown; requires tools/pack.py for full view).
results.summary: Per-target-data tick routine that updates cached target velocity/closing-speed classification buckets and several visibility/awareness flags used by later targeting logic; only partially inspected due to truncation.

results.name: actor_target_scan_potential_targets
results.evidence: Builds a PVS/visibility bitmask for the actor's cluster or its encounter squad's clusters, then iterates the actor's linked target-data list (actor+0x50) checking each target's combat state, distance, and visibility bit before further processing; calls object_get_root_parent_placement and qsort; body largely truncated (341 lines not shown).
results.summary: Large per-actor tick routine that scans and re-ranks the actor's known potential targets using cluster visibility bitmasks and distance/state checks, allocating/deleting target-data records as needed; only partially inspected due to truncation.

results.name: actor_target_evaluate_squad_link
results.evidence: Walks a squad member's target-object linked chain via param_2 (object+0xc-stride, offset 0x14 'next'), calling actor_get_firing_positions and object_get_position for each entry and comparing danger-radius overlap against actor_get_firing_positions results, calling FUN_0041ec90 (actor_danger_register_point) when a hazard is found; body truncated (137 lines not shown).
results.summary: Iterates a squad's shared target/danger linked list registering nearby danger points and evaluating visibility/engagement eligibility against each entry; only partially inspected due to truncation.

results.name: actor_danger_register_stationary_object
results.evidence: Checks an object's sign-bit flag at +0x2f0 (grenade/hazard marker) and near-zero velocity (obj[0x1a..0x1c]^2 < 0.0011) to detect a landed hazardous object, then writes the same danger-record layout (offset+0x280 type=3, +0x28c object index, +0x294 radius, +0x298.. position, +0x2a4.. velocity) used by actor_danger_register_point.
results.summary: Detects a stationary hazardous object (e.g. a landed grenade) near the actor and, if it outranks the currently tracked danger, registers it as the actor's active danger record.

results.name: actor_danger_register_point
results.evidence: Compares an incoming danger radius+10 against an existing distance param_2 and the actor's stored danger priority at actor+0x2d4; if it wins, zeroes the danger-record block (actor+0x280, 0x6c bytes), stamps type=1, object index, radius, and fetches position via object_get_position into +0x2a4/0x2a8/0x2ac.
results.summary: Registers a point-source danger (e.g. an explosion or thrown grenade) as the actor's active danger record if it is closer or takes priority over the currently tracked one.

results.name: actor_danger_update
results.evidence: Requires an active danger record (actor+0x280>=1), refetches the tracked object via object_try_and_get, recomputes distance/bounding-box fields at +0x2b0..0x2e4, then branches on record type (sVar7==1 stealth-object case using FUN_0043ea80/FUN_00564390, sVar7==2 registered-object case calling FUN_0041bb30/FUN_0042b270); tail truncated (81 lines not shown).
results.summary: Per-tick refresh of the actor's currently active danger record: re-resolves the danger object's position, recomputes derived bounding/aim data, and drives follow-up reactions depending on the danger's type.

results.name: actor_target_has_conflicting_neighbor
results.evidence: Walks the actor's own target-data linked list (actor+0x50 chain, stride 0x138) looking for another entry sharing the same tracked object/group (+0x18/+0x1c) or overlapping in combat state (2..5), within 2.5m planar distance, <1.5 height difference, and >0.5 direction dot product.
results.summary: Checks whether the given target-data entry (param_1) has another target-data entry in the same actor's list that effectively refers to the same nearby threat, used to avoid duplicate target tracking.

results.name: actor_get_relevant_squad_member_target
results.evidence: Iterates a fixed 4-entry recent-attacker table at object+0x438 (stride 16 bytes), resolving each recorded attacker's group leader (obj+0x328/+0x324) through FUN_0043ea80 (a target-data acquire/lookup helper), keeping the highest-scoring valid entry in combat state 2..3.
results.summary: Picks the best (highest-scored, still-combat-relevant) recent-attacker entry from a squad member's fixed attacker-history table and returns its resolved target-data index.

results.name: actor_get_squad_recent_attacker_target
results.evidence: Nearly identical structure to actor_get_relevant_squad_member_target (0x41f550) but iterates the actor's own controlled unit's recent-attacker table (object+0x430) via object_try_and_get and FUN_0043ea80, keeping the entry in combat state 2..3 with the highest score.
results.summary: Selects the best recent-attacker entry from the actor's controlled unit's own attacker-history table, returning its resolved target-data index.

results.name: actor_target_data_acquire
results.evidence: Resolves or creates a target-data record for an object via FUN_0043eb30/FUN_0043e910/FUN_0043e980, merges tracked-node fields when a target moves between squad-member owners, then calls actor_rate_potential_target to score the new/updated record.
results.summary: Finds or allocates the actor's target-data record for a given object/unit, migrating tracked-node state when ownership changes, and rescoring it via actor_rate_potential_target.

results.name: actor_target_mark_engaged
results.evidence: Sets or clears the engagement timestamp fields at target-data+0x9c/+0xa0 using the global tick counter DAT_006f1d6c based on param_1, then calls unit_update_active_combat_flag and rescoring via actor_rate_potential_target.
results.summary: Marks or unmarks a target-data record as currently 'engaged' by stamping an engagement timer, then refreshes the associated unit's active-combat flag and target score.

results.name: actor_set_target_alert_flag_low
results.evidence: Sets unit-record byte at offset 0xb9 for a valid unit index (in_ECX); if that unit is the actor's currently watched target (actor+0x270), calls actor_update_target_combat_status and actor_update_awareness_level.
results.summary: Sets a low-tier alert flag (+0xb9) on the given unit, and if it is the actor's current watched target, refreshes the actor's combat-status and awareness state.

results.name: actor_set_target_alert_flag_medium
results.evidence: Byte-for-byte identical to actor_set_target_alert_flag_low (0x41fb00) except it writes unit+0xba instead of +0xb9, part of a sequential trio of near-duplicate flag setters (0xb9/0xba/0xbb).
results.summary: Sets a medium-tier alert flag (+0xba) on the given unit, and if it is the actor's current watched target, refreshes the actor's combat-status and awareness state.

results.name: actor_set_target_alert_flag_high
results.evidence: Largest of the 0xb9/0xba/0xbb trio: for a valid unit sets unit+0xbb and additionally promotes a combat-state-4 unit record (unit+0x24) to state 5; for the sentinel case (in_EDX==-1) instead clears several actor perception fields (+0x3c4,+0x3bc,+0x3bd,+0x72,+0x74) and calls actor_update_awareness_level.
results.summary: Sets a high-tier alert flag (+0xbb) on a unit and promotes its combat state from 4 to 5, or, when called with no unit, resets the actor's own perception/search timers and refreshes awareness.

results.name: unit_update_active_combat_flag
results.evidence: Computes whether a unit is currently 'active' in combat (state field +0x24 in 2..3, exposed +0x60!=0, not dead +0x127==0, and either seen by its actor's watched target, aiming (+0x135/+0x136), or being controlled (+0x10==0xf)), stores the result at unit+0xa4, and clears aim-smoothing fields when it drops to inactive.
results.summary: Recomputes and stores whether a unit should be treated as 'actively' engaged in combat this tick, clearing cached aim-timer fields and a related actor perception counter when it becomes inactive.

results.name: actor_get_ranged_attack_vector
results.evidence: For a vehicle unit (unit+0x12e set) copies a seat/hardpoint position from obj+0x23c/0x240/0x244 into param_1; otherwise, if the unit already has a firing point (+0x1c != -1) delegates to FUN_004281f0; otherwise loops the actor's perceived-unit list checking that no ally lies within 0.5 dot-product alignment of the intended fire direction (friendly-fire clearance check).
results.summary: Determines the actor's ranged-attack aim position/vector, either from a vehicle hardpoint, a cached firing point, or by checking that no ally blocks the intended line of fire.

results.name: actor_evaluate_flank_offset
results.evidence: Pure geometry helper operating on register-passed float vectors: computes a 2D perpendicular basis from in_ECX, projects an enemy-relative offset (unaff_ESI - unaff_EDI) onto it, optionally mirrors the offset into an output vector (unaff_EBX), and classifies the result into a small tier (0/1/2) based on distance-squared thresholds (0.36/1.21) and a z-component range check.
results.summary: Computes a flanking offset/side position relative to a target direction and classifies it into a coarse tier used to rank candidate flanking allies.

results.name: actor_scale_value_by_ally_exposure
results.evidence: Walks the actor's perceived-unit list counting allies of the same type (matching actor+4) that are either exposed-but-idle (sVar7, unit+300 'aiming' flag) or already alert/vehicle-aiming (sVar2, via ally-actor+0x308/+0x6c/+0xa8), then scales *param_1 by a factor derived from those counts (clamped to [0.0, 2.0]).
results.summary: Scales an input value (e.g. a suppression or alert threshold) up or down depending on how many nearby allies are already exposed and engaging or alert, clamped to a 0-2x range.

results.name: ai_group_bucket_find_or_add
results.evidence: Linear-searches a fixed stride-0x1c array (in_EAX) of up to param_1 live entries (tracked by *unaff_EDI) for a matching key (unaff_EBX); if absent and space remains, appends a freshly-initialized bucket entry (several -1 sentinels and a 0x7f7fffff FLT_MAX field) and returns its index.
results.summary: Finds the bucket index matching a given key in a small fixed-capacity array, or allocates and initializes a new bucket for it if space remains.

results.name: unit_get_combat_priority
results.evidence: For a unit in active combat (state +0x24 in 2..3) with the 'active' flag unit+0xa4 set, returns tiered priority values: 4 if fleeing (+0x74), 2 or 3 if vehicle-aiming (+0x12f, based on +0x122<2), or 1 if currently attacking (+0x32>1), else 0.
results.summary: Returns a small combat-priority tier (0-4) for a unit, used to rank allies when deciding who needs backup or grouping.

results.name: actor_scan_allies_for_backup_request
results.evidence: Iterates the actor's perceived-unit list; for allies with an unresolved combat priority whose controlling actor has an active backup request (ally_actor+0x3a8 nonzero, +0x3ac valid) within range, resolves the requester via FUN_0043ea80, buckets it by unit_get_combat_priority into fixed slots via ai_group_bucket_find_or_add, tracking the nearest per bucket; remainder truncated (20 lines not shown).
results.summary: Scans nearby allies for outstanding backup requests and groups the closest eligible requester per combat-priority bucket for the actor to consider responding to.

results.name: actor_update_combat_tactics_state
results.evidence: Per-actor tick routine: conditionally calls actor_set_combat_alert_flag, exponentially smooths an accuracy-like value (actor+0x350 target, +0x354 smoothed) via f2xm1/fscale, broadcasts a state-change event via ai_communication_broadcast when +0x1c9 changes, then loops the perceived-unit list calling actor_get_ranged_attack_vector and actor_evaluate_flank_offset to find and record a flanking ally via actor_scan_allies_for_backup_request; body truncated (130 lines not shown).
results.summary: Large per-actor combat tick routine that updates alert state, smooths an accuracy value over time, broadcasts squad notifications, and evaluates nearby allies for flanking/charge opportunities; only partially inspected due to truncation.

results.name: actor_queue_search_position
results.evidence: Only updates when the actor is not deep in combat (actor+0x6a<3) and the new priority (in_DX) is >= the stored priority at actor+0x312; records an optional 3-float position (in_ECX) at +0x318, an optional 3-float direction (unaff_ESI) at +0x330, plus scalar payload fields at +0x33c/0x340/0x344/0x348.
results.summary: Queues a candidate search position/direction for the actor to investigate later, replacing the current one only if the new request has equal or higher priority and the actor is not already in deep combat.

results.name: actor_queue_look_position
results.evidence: Smaller sibling of actor_queue_search_position: updates actor+0x2ee (priority) only if the new priority (in_DX) is strictly greater, storing a single position payload (param_1 and optional in_ECX 3-float vector) at +0x2f4/+0x2fc.
results.summary: Queues a single look-at position/target for the actor if the given priority beats the currently queued one.

results.name: actor_evaluate_target_visibility
results.evidence: For units in active combat with sufficient awareness (actor+0x6a>1, +0x544<5), fetches a per-target datum via datum_get and applies a decaying re-notice cooldown (datum+0x5c/+0x58) gated by a 600-tick window, then queues a dialogue/queue event (actor+0x544=4) with a random duration scaled by random_real_range; second half evaluates look-priority via actor_queue_look_position; tail truncated (35 lines not shown).
results.summary: Evaluates whether the actor should react to becoming visible to/from a given target unit, applying a re-notice cooldown, queuing a reaction dialogue event, and updating the actor's queued look position.

results.name: actor_record_perception_event
results.evidence: Keeps the maximum of a priority value (in_DX) against actor+0x34a, storing the associated data pointer (unaff_ESI) at actor+0x34c; on a tie, merges by taking the larger of the two data values.
results.summary: Records a perception event's priority and associated data on the actor, keeping only the highest-priority (or larger-valued, on ties) event seen this tick.

results.name: actor_notify_target_engaged
results.evidence: When a candidate unit's target (resolved via unit's controlling actor+0x18) is not dead (+0x127==0) and the candidate unit is exposed (+0x60!=0), calls ai_communication_broadcast with code 5-(in_DL!=0).
results.summary: Notifies a target's controlling actor via a squad broadcast event that the given unit has become an exposed threat/engagement, choosing between two event codes based on in_DL.

results.name: actor_start_search_timer
results.evidence: Stamps actor+0x3a0 with the current tick count (DAT_006f1d6c+0xc), calls actor_target_get_relationship_object, and queues a search position via actor_queue_search_position with a fixed priority (0x3fc00000 = 1.5) and duration (0x5a = 90 ticks).
results.summary: Starts (or restarts) the actor's search timer and queues a fixed-priority search position around the current target's relationship object.

results.name: actor_clear_search_queue
results.evidence: Trivial one-line wrapper that calls actor_queue_search_position(0xffffffff, 0, 0x5a), the sentinel pattern used elsewhere in this file to reset the queued search position.
results.summary: Clears/resets the actor's queued search position by submitting the sentinel 'no position' request.

results.name: actor_clear_search_and_reevaluate_look
results.evidence: Calls actor_clear_search_queue, then if the unit referenced by unit+0x1c has a positive field at controlling-actor+0x74 it calls actor_record_perception_event to notify the actor of a perception update.
results.summary: Clears the actor's queued search position and, if the associated unit's controlling actor currently has a pending flee/alert value, records a perception event for it.

results.name: actor_queue_dialogue_direction_or_point
results.evidence: Accepts either an explicit direction vector (in_EAX, normalized/negated) or a target-data index (in_ECX); gates on actor combat state (+0x6a) and a pending-event counter cap (+0x544<0xc), then queues an event (type 4 or 1) with a duration derived from random_real_range and a lookup table (DAT_00655654) into fields +0x544..0x558.
results.summary: Queues a directional or positional combat-reaction dialogue/event for the actor with a randomized duration, choosing event type based on whether a direction vector or a target index was supplied.

results.name: actor_queue_dialogue_with_cooldown
results.evidence: Uses the same datum_get + re-notice-cooldown gating (target datum+0x5c/+0x58, 600-tick window) as actor_evaluate_target_visibility (0x421c20), but on success queues event type 5 (actor+0x544=5) with a random duration from random_real_range and table DAT_0065563c.
results.summary: Queues a cooldown-gated combat-reaction dialogue event (type 5) for a given target, reusing the same per-target re-notice throttling used elsewhere.

results.name: actor_queue_dialogue_position
results.evidence: Only runs when the actor is not idle (actor+0x6a!=1); forwards a 3-component position (in_EAX[0..2]) into the shared event-queue fields with event type 3 (actor+0x544=3), gated by a pending-event cap (+0x544<2) and awareness field (+1000<7), with duration from random_real_range and table DAT_0065562c.
results.summary: Queues a position-based combat-reaction dialogue event (type 3) for the actor with a randomized duration, but only while the actor is not idle.

results.name: actor_notify_and_queue_dialogue_direction
results.evidence: Computes a facing/aim direction relative to actor+0x120; if no active danger record matches param_2 it calls actor_queue_look_position and actor_clear_search_queue, otherwise broadcasts event 10 via ai_communication_broadcast; afterward queues a positional dialogue event (type 3) as in actor_queue_dialogue_position.
results.summary: Reacts to a directional stimulus by either broadcasting a squad notification (if it matches the actor's existing tracked danger) or updating the queued look position, then queues a follow-up positional dialogue event.

results.name: actor_notify_and_queue_dialogue_point
results.evidence: Mirrors actor_notify_and_queue_dialogue_direction: normalizes param_3 relative to actor+0x120, calls actor_queue_look_position and actor_clear_search_queue, conditionally calls actor_record_perception_event via FUN_0045bd50, then queues a positional dialogue event (type 6) with a randomized duration from table DAT_00655640.
results.summary: Reacts to a point-source stimulus (e.g. a grenade or explosion location) by updating the actor's look position/search state and queuing a corresponding dialogue event (type 6).

results.name: actor_notify_unit_state_change
results.evidence: Branches on whether the controlled unit (param_1) is alive (+0x60): if so, calls actor_clear_search_and_reevaluate_look and, depending on whether the unit has a vehicle seat (+0x218) or a weapon (+500), calls FUN_00428420 or actor_target_data_acquire (0x41f7d0); if dead, queues a search position via actor_queue_search_position; afterward queues dialogue event type 7 via the shared cooldown/queue pattern.
results.summary: Handles a change in the controlled unit's alive/vehicle/weapon state, updating the actor's look/search targets accordingly and queuing a corresponding dialogue event (type 7).

results.name: actor_update_search_target_for_unit
results.evidence: Marks actor+0x8d as processed for unit param_1; when the unit is not exposed (unit+0x60==0), resolves its best 'aim' target via actor_get_relevant_squad_member_target (FUN_0041f550) and, based on a random roll and actor_scale_value_by_ally_exposure, stores it at actor+0x30c with priority actor+0x308.
results.summary: For a hidden/unexposed unit, picks a relevant recent-attacker target and, with some randomized and ally-exposure-scaled probability, records it as the actor's next investigation/search target.

results.name: actor_request_backup_for_unit
results.evidence: When a unit is not exposed and its controlled object recently took damage (object flags bit 0x20, obj+0x39c stale-time check), rolls a probability via actor_scale_value_by_ally_exposure/random_real, and if it beats the roll, records a backup-request target (actor+0x30c, priority actor+0x308=2), resolving via FUN_0043ea80 if the unit is in a turret seat.
results.summary: Requests backup for a unit that was recently damaged while hidden, with the request probability scaled by nearby ally exposure.

results.name: actor_notify_grenade_or_threat_direction
results.evidence: If the actor has a valid cluster/squad leader link (actor+0x18), remaps param_2 (0/1/2) to a squad-event value and calls ai_communication_broadcast with code 0xb when param_1==2, then normalizes a direction vector and conditionally calls actor_queue_look_position before clearing the search queue via actor_queue_search_position(0xffffffff,...).
results.summary: Notifies the actor's squad of a directional threat (such as an incoming grenade) via a broadcast event, and updates the actor's queued look/search state accordingly.

results.name: actor_notify_squad_event_and_search
results.evidence: If the actor has a cluster leader (actor+0x18 valid), calls ai_communication_broadcast with code 0x17 or 0x16 depending on in_CL; if param_1 is set and no higher-priority search is already queued (actor+0x308<6), records a generic search request (actor+0x308=6, actor+0x30c=0xffffffff).
results.summary: Broadcasts a squad-level notification event and optionally queues a generic (targetless) search request for the actor.

results.name: actor_boost_accuracy_after_alert
results.evidence: Only runs while actor+0x358 is set and the actor definition's field at offset 0x334 (via the actor-type pointer) is positive; clears the flag, computes a duration via __ftol into actor+0x35a, and if the watched target (actor+0x270) is close (<4.0) boosts the smoothed accuracy value at actor+0x354 to at least 1.8/0x3fe66666.
results.summary: After certain alert transitions, temporarily boosts the actor's smoothed accuracy value when its watched target is nearby, for a duration derived from the actor's definition data.

results.name: actor_evaluate_charge_trigger
results.evidence: Uses actor_get_actor_definition and FUN_00569c90 to gate on the actor being in a valid melee/charge-eligible state (awareness>=5, distance thresholds from definition fields +0x74/+0xa0/+0x16c), then probabilistically decides via random_seed_global whether to trigger a charge, adjusted by counting nearby allies already charging vs. not (actor+0x362); body truncated (52 lines not shown).
results.summary: Decides whether the actor should initiate a melee/charge action against its current target based on distance thresholds, awareness level, and a randomized roll weighted by how many nearby allies are already charging; only partially inspected due to truncation.

results.name: actor_pick_dialogue_variant_a
results.evidence: Advances the shared RNG stream (random_seed_global) only when in_AX is 1, 2, or 3, then returns a value from __ftol clamped to [0,0xff], matching a 'pick sound/line variant index' pattern.
results.summary: Picks a randomized dialogue/sound variant index (0-255), re-rolling the RNG only for certain input categories (1, 2, or 3).

results.name: actor_pick_dialogue_variant_b
results.evidence: Near-identical to actor_pick_dialogue_variant_a but advances the RNG for in_AX==1 or 1<in_AX<4 (i.e. 2 or 3) treated as a single case, otherwise returning the same clamped __ftol result.
results.summary: Variant of actor_pick_dialogue_variant_a with slightly different RNG-advance grouping, returning a clamped (0-255) dialogue/sound variant index.

results.name: swarm_component_compute_avoidance_offset
results.evidence: Walks the swarm entry referenced by actor+0x28 (DAT_0088035c array, stride 0x98) looking for the swarm-component slot matching param_2 (stride 0x40 array off DAT_00880358), then, depending on component state flags at +0x21, either computes a facing-based offset via vector2d_normalize_with_length or calls FUN_004beb30 to derive an avoidance vector written to param_4.
results.summary: Computes a per-component avoidance or facing offset vector for a swarm creature (e.g. Flood infection form) based on its swarm-component state, writing the result through param_4.

results.name: actor_initialize_unit_ai_properties
results.evidence: Copies AI-relevant fields from the unit's type definition (puVar2, via DAT_0087bc14 tag-index table) into the live unit object: shield/stun thresholds via object_initialize_shield_stun_thresholds, notice range at +0x176, up to 4 randomized color variants via color_interpolate, and attaches child objects (grenades/weapons) via object_new_with_datum_role_control and object_placement_data_initialize.
results.summary: Initializes a newly spawned unit's AI-relevant runtime fields (shield thresholds, notice range, color variation, and attached weapon/grenade child objects) from its tag definition.

results.name: actor_spawn_additional_units
results.evidence: Loops in_DX times, each iteration re-rolling random_seed_global, deriving a spawn angle from object_placement_data_initialize plus fcos/fsin, fetching a base position via object_get_position, creating a new object via object_new, initializing it via FUN_00426cf0 (actor_initialize_unit_ai_properties), and attaching an actor to it via actor_new_and_attach_to_unit.
results.summary: Spawns a requested number of additional units at randomized angles/positions around a reference unit and attaches a new actor to each successfully created unit.

results.name: actor_broadcast_value_to_controlled_units
results.evidence: Writes a caller-supplied value (unaff_SI) into object+0xb8 for either the actor's single controlled unit (actor+0x18) when it has no cluster (actor+6==0), or for every member of its unit cluster linked list (actor+0x24 chain) or encounter squad array (DAT_0088035c) otherwise.
results.summary: Broadcasts a 16-bit value into a field (offset +0xb8) on every unit controlled by the actor, whether it controls a single unit, a linked unit cluster, or a full encounter squad.

results.name: actor_set_active_flag
results.evidence: Compares the requested state (in_AL) against the actor's stored active flag at actor+8; deactivating tears down search state (FUN_00427e00), deletes any swarm (actor_delete_swarm), and calls actor_set_units_active; activating creates a swarm if the actor has a cluster (actor+6!=0) via actor_create_swarm.
results.summary: Activates or deactivates the actor, creating or tearing down its swarm and clearing search state as appropriate, and propagating the active flag to its controlled unit(s).

results.name: actor_link_to_unit_cluster
results.evidence: Inserts actor (param_1) at the head of unit (param_2)'s cluster linked list (unit+0x1f8 head, actor+0x1fc/+0x200 next/prev links), allocating a swarm-component datum first via datum_new when the actor has a swarm (actor+0x28!=-1), then calls swarm_add_component, actor_remove_from_unit_cluster/actor_unlink_unit for any prior links, and object_mark_pending_delete for orphaned objects.
results.summary: Links an actor to a unit's cluster (linked list of controlling actors for a single physical unit, e.g. a swarm/Flood combined form), replacing any prior linkage and registering a swarm component if applicable.

results.name: actor_clear_perceived_unit_list
results.evidence: Loops while the actor's perceived-unit list head (actor+0x50) is non-empty, calling actor_replace_object_reference then FUN_0043ea20 and datum_delete on each entry until the list is empty.
results.summary: Frees every entry in the actor's perceived-unit (target-data) linked list, deleting each associated datum.

results.name: actor_cache_swarm_member_position
results.evidence: Looks up a unit via DAT_008603b0, tests its health/death field (+0xb4==0), selects its death-position pointer (+0x4d8) or the sentinel -1, calls object_get_position(), and stores the resulting position into a swarm-entry slot (DAT_00880358 array, stride 0x40, +0x10).
results.summary: Caches a swarm member's current (or, if dead, last-death) position into its swarm-entry slot for later avoidance/formation calculations.

results.name: actor_is_ranged_burst_active
results.evidence: Checks actor+0x6a==3 (a combat sub-state) and actor+0x72 < actor+0x6e (current burst count vs. its limit) before returning a packed boolean, matching the burst-length fields also referenced by actor_should_end_burst (0x4281b0).
results.summary: Returns true if the actor is currently in the middle of an active ranged-attack burst that has not yet reached its length limit.

results.name: actor_should_end_burst
results.evidence: Tests actor+0x6e>6 together with mode field +0x6c==4 and a secondary counter +0xa8>0, sharing the same burst-length field (+0x6e) referenced by actor_is_ranged_burst_active (0x428180).
results.summary: Determines whether the actor's current attack burst has run long enough (and is in the right sub-mode) that it should be ended.
